_comment: External (non-package-manager) dependencies this codebase tracks pinned versions/commits of. check_dependency_releases.py reads this file and reports when upstream has moved past the pinned point. 'release' mode compares against GitHub's latest-release tag; 'branch' mode compares against a tracked branch's current HEAD commit (used when we deliberately build from a branch other than the default, e.g. a bug fix that only landed on 'develop'). IMPORTANT: 'pinned' means the last version this codebase's own real test suite was actually run against and confirmed working -- not whatever happens to be currently installed/deployed, and never a value copied from a fresh API query without also re-running the tests against it. Bump 'pinned' only after a real verification pass.

kopia.notes: Bumped 2026-08-27 (Bruce: bump all three before deployment). Verified by downloading the real v0.23.1 release tarball, computing its sha256 directly, confirming the archive's internal layout (kopia-0.23.1-linux-x64/kopia) still matches extract_member='kopia', and running the extracted binary (`kopia --version` reports 0.23.1 correctly). No live network-download test exists in this codebase for kopia -- binary_downloader's own test suite mocks urlopen with a self-built tarball -- so this direct download+checksum+run is the real verification pass.

etcd.notes: Bumped 2026-08-27 (Bruce: bump all three before deployment). Verified by downloading the real v3.7.1 release tarball, computing its sha256 directly, confirming etcd-v3.7.1-linux-amd64/etcd still exists in the archive matching extract_member='etcd', and running the extracted binary (`etcd --version` reports 3.7.1 correctly). Same caveat as kopia: no live network-download test exists for etcd in this codebase, so this direct download+checksum+run is the real verification pass.

cloudflared.notes: Bumped 2026-09-14 from 2026.8.3 (Bruce: update dependencies when you can), skipping 2026.9.0. Reviewed the real changelog via `gh api repos/cloudflare/cloudflared/compare/2026.8.3...2026.9.1` (14 commits): Go toolchain bump to 1.26.8, removal of upstream's vendor/ directory (build-side only), an access-token lock self-deadlock fix during same-process reauth, edge registration error propagation over QUIC, staged-but-unregistered protected Quick Tunnel plumbing (no new user-reachable flag), and distroless Docker digest bumps. The one potentially breaking item: 2026.9.0 removed the `--transport-loglevel` flag outright, and 2026.9.1 reverted that to deprecated-not-removed (so clients still passing it keep starting) and added a formal 3-month breaking-change notice policy to upstream's README/AGENTS.md. Checked this codebase's real consumer of this manifest entry: it is pager_duty/daemon/generalized_monitor.py, which runs `cloudflared tunnel info <target>` (cloudflare/utils/cloudflare_daemon.py loads the separately vendored libcloudflared.so, not this binary). `grep -rn transport-loglevel` across hams_open (excluding the vendored daemons/cloudflared source) finds no use, and `cloudflared tunnel info --help` on the new binary still documents the same subcommand and positional TUNNEL argument -- so this release is non-breaking for this codebase. Verified the binary itself: downloaded the real 2026.9.1 cloudflared-linux-amd64 release asset (39838488 bytes), computed its sha256 directly (03f1f25d1cc93b9ad6c60569d44060bc4f17ed97075760ed8cfca4b12dcd68cc), which matches both the asset digest GitHub's release API publishes and the checksum list in the release notes, and ran it (`cloudflared --version` reports `2026.9.1 (built 2026-09-11-13:35 UTC)`). Same caveat as kopia/etcd: no live network-download test exists for cloudflared in this codebase, so this direct download+checksum+run is the real verification pass. binary_manifest.json and binary_manifest_data.xml both updated and re-verified in sync via check_binary_manifest_consistency.py. Previous bump, 2026-09-03: dependency-watch.yml surfaced this pin as stale once its own real submodule-checkout bug was fixed (see night_shift_todo.md). 2026.8.3 is a small, low-risk single-version bump whose real changelog (checked via `gh api .../compare`, not assumed) is mostly internal cleanup plus one real security fix: `chore: bump gorilla/websocket for GO-2026-6278` (GHSA-w67g-5rqw-f597, High severity -- a cryptographically weak PRNG in gorilla/websocket's own WebSocket frame-masking, fixed upstream in gorilla/websocket v1.5.3). Verified the same way as the prior bump: downloaded the real 2026.8.3 raw binary release asset, computed its sha256 directly (f29324fe934d1e100617484c78deef803c4dc2cd351d645bbde42e96b4fccc5e, matching the checksum GitHub's own release page publishes for this asset), and ran it (`cloudflared --version` reports `2026.8.3 (built 2026-08-31-10:04 UTC)` correctly). Same caveat as kopia/etcd: no live network-download test exists for cloudflared in this codebase, so this direct download+checksum+run is the real verification pass. binary_manifest.json and binary_manifest_data.xml both updated and re-verified in sync via check_binary_manifest_consistency.py (see that script's own doc comment for the real bug this guards against).

ardopcf.pinned_via: hams_com daemons/hams_local_relay/install_relay_runtime_deps.sh and install_relay_runtime_deps_rpm.sh ARDOPCF_COMMIT (built at exactly this commit); consumed by daemons/hams_local_relay/src/ardop.rs find_ardopcf_binary()/spawn_ardopcf()
ardopcf.notes: Bumped 2026-09-14 from 346b0c5a (Bruce: update dependencies when you can). Reviewed `gh api repos/pflarue/ardop/compare/346b0c5a...c1e11ef5`: 3 commits, all 'clarify licensing' -- +24 lines of license-header comments each in lib/txt2c/txt2c.c, lib/ws_server/ws_server.c and lib/ws_server/ws_server.h, no code change, nothing touching the CLI flags, host-command port, or startup behavior spawn_ardopcf()/wait_for_ardopcf_ready() use. Verified for real anyway: cloned develop at c1e11ef5 and ran plain `make` exactly as install_relay_runtime_deps.sh does (exit 0, zero warnings, zero errors); the binary's `-h` banner reads `ardopcf Version 1.0.4.1.3_develop_linux`; ran it with the exact spawn_ardopcf() flags (`ardopcf <port> null null -l <dir> -G 0`) and confirmed it accepted a TCP connection on the host port within ~1.8s, listened only on <port> and <port>+1 (no 8514 WebGui socket, so -G 0 still suppresses it), logged `Terminating on signal: SIGTERM` and exited 0 on TERM. Ran the real `cargo test --release ardop -- --test-threads=1` suite in daemons/hams_local_relay (hams_com e33f3ff9 plus another agent's uncommitted toolchain/source edits in the tree) with the new binary PATH-overridden ahead of the Aug-26 /usr/local/bin/ardopcf, twice: 7 passed, 0 failed both times, including spawn_ardopcf_and_wait_for_ardopcf_ready_against_the_real_built_binary (with --nocapture, no 'skipping' line) and winlink's real pat-connect-over-ardop test. A process watcher during the run recorded the spawned child's /proc/<pid>/exe as the freshly built scratch binary itself, so the real-binary test exercised this build, not the installed one and not a silent skip. /usr/local/bin/ardopcf was not updated in place; the next run of install_relay_runtime_deps.sh (always a fresh clone of develop HEAD) picks this up. Standing rationale: deliberately tracking 'develop', not 'master' or the latest numbered release -- master still has a known, already-fixed-upstream build bug (GCC14 rejects lib/rawhid/rawhid.c's pointer/int mismatch; see pflarue/ardop issues #124 and #162) that was never merged from develop to master. See check-upstream-issues-before-filing lesson before assuming any future ardopcf build error is novel.

mercury.pinned_via: hams_com daemons/hams_local_relay/install_relay_runtime_deps.sh and install_relay_runtime_deps_rpm.sh MERCURY_COMMIT (built at exactly this commit); consumed by daemons/hams_local_relay/src/mercury.rs find_mercury_binary()/spawn_mercury()
mercury.notes: Bumped 2026-09-15 from e5b0044b to 44621de6: `gh api repos/Rhizomatica/mercury/compare/e5b0044b...44621de6` shows only docs/ARQ.md and docs/README.md changed, so the e5b0044b verification below applies unchanged. The install scripts now build exactly this commit (they used to clone the moving branch HEAD). GPL-3.0, run as an isolated subprocess (see DATAC_TRANSPORT_INTEGRATION.md's GPL-isolation section) -- never linked into hams_local_relay itself, so a version bump here is a pure behavior/compatibility question, not a licensing one. Bumped 2026-09-14 from e65bdeaf (Bruce: update dependencies when you can); the watch run reported 770b964e, but mercuryv2 had already moved again, so this pins the newer HEAD e5b0044b. Reviewed `gh api repos/Rhizomatica/mercury/compare/e65bdeaf...e5b0044b` (87 commits, 0 behind): a new MFSK waveform (DSP core under modem/mfsk/, not yet wired in), ARQ fixes (ACCEPT only for a heard CALL, TURN_REQ tie-break and collision avoidance, DATA accepted while awaiting a keepalive reply), a compiled-out-of-release ARQ trace ring, broadcast RaptorQ symbol-size and listener-shutdown fixes, CoreAudio/GUI work, Makefile header-dependency tracking, and a new Makefile preflight that fails early if <hamlib/rig.h> is unusable. Integration surface checked directly: main.c only gained an ARQ_TRACE_DUMP no-op at shutdown; common/mercury_cli.c only moved the mode table to the new common/mercury_modes.c; `mercury -h` on the new binary still documents `-x null`, `-p <arq_tcp_base_port>` (control = base, data = base+1) and `-L <path>` unchanged; the control-port protocol only gained an additive `MODE [index]` command (OK/BUSY/WRONG replies), with every existing command untouched. One real startup-behavior change: a new persistent chat-history message store ([store] enabled defaults to true) now creates $XDG_STATE_HOME/mercury/messages.jsonl, else $HOME/.local/state/mercury/messages.jsonl, on every start. No CLI flag disables it (only a `-C` INI file with [store] enabled=false), and an init failure is a non-fatal warning, so spawn_mercury() is unaffected -- but the relay's mercury child now leaves a file under the daemon user's home (confirmed: the test run below created /home/bruce/.local/state/mercury/messages.jsonl, 0 bytes). Built for real: cloned mercuryv2 at e5b0044b, applied install_relay_runtime_deps.sh's `sed -i 's/rigerror2(ret)/rigerror(ret)/' radio_io/radio_io.c` (still needed: it still matches exactly one call site, radio_io.c:187, and the Ubuntu 22.04 libhamlib rationale is unchanged; this dev box's libhamlib 4.6.2 exports rigerror2, so the 22.04 link failure itself can't be reproduced here), then ran plain `make`: exit 0, the new hamlib header preflight passed, 7 warning lines (snprintf-truncation/type-limits in unrelated files), no errors. Ran the binary with the exact spawn_mercury() flags (`-x null -p <port> -L <log>`): accepted a TCP connection on the control port within ~0.2s, listened on <port>, <port>+1 and the default broadcast port 8100 (that broadcast listener predates this bump), logged `Mercury engine initialised`, then `Mercury engine shut down` and exit 0 on TERM. Ran the real `cargo test --release mercury -- --test-threads=1` suite in daemons/hams_local_relay (hams_com e33f3ff9 plus another agent's uncommitted toolchain/source edits in the tree) with the new binary PATH-overridden ahead of the Aug-26 /usr/local/bin/mercury: 5 passed, 0 failed, including spawn_mercury_and_wait_for_mercury_ready_against_the_real_built_binary (with --nocapture, no 'skipping' line) and winlink's real pat-connect-over-varahf test. An earlier attempt was killed by an external SIGTERM (cargo exit 143) before any test ran, during concurrent toolchain work on the box, and is not counted. The suite was then re-run twice, 5/5 both times; the second re-run went through a logging exec wrapper, which recorded the tests invoking this build directly (`-x null -p 18300 -L /tmp/mercury_test_<pid>_spawn/mercury.log`, `-x null -p 8300 -L winlink_mercury/mercury.log`, plus `-h` probes), so the real-binary tests exercised e5b0044b, not the installed binary and not a silent skip. /usr/local/bin/mercury was not updated in place; the next run of install_relay_runtime_deps.sh/install_relay_runtime_deps_rpm.sh (always a fresh clone and build) picks this up. Previous bump, 2026-09-05, from 56905a4c: a 28-commit gap: real feature work (macOS DMG code-signing/notarization CI, a Fyne GUI runtime ALSA/PulseAudio subsystem-switch feature, a broadcast chat-length cap fix) mixed with docs/CI churn, none of it touched by this pin's own real integration surface -- confirmed directly via `git diff --stat` restricted to *.c/*.h between the two commits: every changed file lives under audioio/ (the new GUI subsystem-switch feature) or gui_interface/ (the Fyne GUI bridge), except one pure rename in common/cfg_utils.c (`parse_sound_system` made non-static as `cfg_sound_system_parse`, zero behavior change) -- nothing in main.c's own CLI argument parsing or the ARQ/control-port networking code the headless `-x null` backend uses. Verified for real, not just diffed, the same way as the prior bump: cloned mercuryv2 at e65bdeaf and ran the actual `make` build (clean, only three pre-existing snprintf-truncation/type-limit warnings in unrelated files, no errors); ran the resulting binary with the exact flags `spawn_mercury()` uses (`-x null -p <port> -L <log>`) and confirmed it starts, logs "Mercury engine initialised", listens on the control port, accepts a TCP connection the same way `wait_for_mercury_ready()` probes for, and shuts down cleanly on a TERM signal; ran the real `cargo test --release mercury -- --test-threads=1` suite with the new binary PATH-overridden ahead of the still-installed 56905a4c one (same technique the prior bump used) -- 5/5 passed, 0 failed. `-x`/`-p`/`-L` and the control-port protocol are byte-for-byte unchanged from the pinned version's own interface (confirmed against the new binary's own `-h` output, not assumed). System-installed /usr/local/bin/mercury was NOT updated in place (sudo unavailable in this sandbox, same as last time) -- the next real run of install_relay_runtime_deps.sh/install_relay_runtime_deps_rpm.sh (which always clones+builds fresh, never reuses a cached binary) will pick up this new pinned commit on its own.

hamlib.pinned_via: hams_com daemons/hams_local_relay/install_relay_runtime_deps.sh HAMLIB_VERSION/HAMLIB_SHA256 (source fallback for building mercury) and hams_com .github/workflows/build-relay.yml build-windows "Cross-build hamlib for mingw-w64" step HAMLIB_VERSION/HAMLIB_SHA256 (statically linked into the Windows binary, plus a native host build whose rigctl/rotctl --list build.rs bakes into its model tables); otherwise the system package (libhamlib-dev), also referenced by hamlib.rs
hamlib.notes: The distro package is used when it provides every Hamlib 4.x call mercury makes (the install script compiles and links a probe to decide). Where it doesn't (Ubuntu 20.04 ships 3.3, Ubuntu 22.04's 4.3.1 lacks rigerror2), install_relay_runtime_deps.sh builds this pinned release from the checksum-verified release tarball as a static library inside its temporary build directory and links mercury against it (added 2026-09-14 after the ubuntu:20.04 CI leg failed with "'RIG_CAPS_PORT_TYPE' undeclared"). When bumping, update HAMLIB_VERSION and HAMLIB_SHA256 there too (sha256 from the release asset's digest: gh api repos/Hamlib/Hamlib/releases/tags/<version>). When bumping, also update build-relay.yml's build-windows step (same two constants): until 2026-09-15 that step downloaded 4.6.2 with no checksum and outside this watch, and baked its model tables from Ubuntu 24.04's libhamlib-utils 4.5.5 rather than the release it links. When bumping, confirm build.rs's fixed-width `rigctl --list` parser still fits the new release's output (the Windows leg's Build log prints "baked N Hamlib rig model(s)").
